the build this CONTAINER is running, stamped by whoever started it and reported verbatim by GET /api/version. Deliberately NOT derived from the source tree: the answer has to be true of the container, and a container knows nothing about the repo it was built from. The blue/green deploy sets it to the tag it is deploying (PRD decision 39); unset reads as "unknown", so an unstamped deployment simply never offers the terminal's reload bar
the runtime kernel's runtime.v1 surface the dispatcher spawns workers on (+ schedule.v1 for routines)

keys.default: (unset — derived per dispatch: the private baseline only)
keys.description: the ordered THREE-TIER mount STACK the dispatch stamps into the worker spec — a JSON list [{slug,path,role,write,primary}], one entry per mount: _global (RO) + the active workspaces (RW) + _system (RW) (AMENDMENT 4 / WP-A1.1). Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

host path / repo dir of the mandatory GLOBAL SYSTEM workspace (_global), first in EVERY worker stack — behaviour/skills/tools (AMENDMENT 4). A live mount: updating this one repo propagates to all agents next turn. Missing or invalid configuration fails dispatch closed
comma-separated user ids whose workers mount _global READ-WRITE — the admin setup conversation is the one sanctioned writer of the org tier; all other subjects mount it ro
pin the _global mount to a ref (branch/tag/sha) for safe rollout of a global behaviour change; empty = mount HEAD (AMENDMENT 4, Q17)
the authenticated human principal's name the dispatch stamps for per-mount commit attribution (D4: git author = principal, committer = platform). Runtime-injected per dispatch
the authenticated human principal's email for per-mount commit attribution (D4). Runtime-injected per dispatch

keys.default: (empty — FAIL-CLOSED: 401 when the gateway's X-User-Id is absent)
keys.description: single-user fallback subject for a direct/self-host deploy with no gateway in front
the per-dispatch unit:<id>:out/:in streams the control plane relays (SSE) + the transcript tail
the per-subject workspace tree this control plane reads (WorkspaceReader) and seeds

Lane W: seconds a turn-commit waits on the per-shared-workspace write lock (cross-process flock serializing concurrent members' commits, shared/adapters.py) before raising WorkspaceBusyError — bounded so a wedged holder can never stall a workspace forever
the registry of workspace templates (one validated seed per subdir)
explicit, already-resolved seed dir override (tests / special deploys)
which workspace template new subjects are seeded from

the model id every agent turn runs on — the chat turn and the write-back phase alike; the key Settings → Models writes and the dispatch stamps into every worker. Empty means the harness's own default, which exists only for the CLI harnesses: the openai-agent harness has no default host and no default model and refuses the turn with a named-key error rather than asking an endpoint for an empty model

agent harness stamped onto dispatched workspace turns: claude-code (default) | codex (the Codex app-server) | openai-agent (this repo's own loop over any OpenAI-compatible endpoint). The deployment FLOOR only — Settings → Models pins a harness per subject and the dispatch overlay wins. The openai-agent lane is configured by VEXA_LLM_BASE_URL / _API_KEY / _MODEL / _EXTRA_BODY, which the WORKER reads from its dispatch-stamped env: #1415 removed them from the runtime's forward list, so they travel by stamp and never by forwarding
operator gate on workspace-pinned models (comma-separated)

keys.default: (empty — the deployment’s own gateway host(s) plus api.anthropic.com, openrouter.ai and the CCC box)
keys.description: operator allow-list for the base_url a SUBJECT may pin under Settings → Models (comma-separated host globs). A subject-chosen endpoint is an outbound destination picked by a non-operator and the worker carries a model credential to it, so anything unmatched is refused at dispatch with a friction record. Loopback/link-local/private addresses and single-label docker service names (redis, admin-api) need an EXACT literal entry — a wildcard never reaches the deployment’s own network
chat worker warm-serve window after its last turn (s) — a follow-up inside it lands on the warm worker
tool.v1 descriptors + MCP launch specs a unit's tools resolve against
workspace-authored routines reconcile interval (0 disables the reconciler)
brokered, scoped identity the worker presents (ADR-0003)
the shared key per-dispatch tokens are signed with (dev tier; k8s → SPIRE behind the same seam)
the gateway base URL for 'add bot from URL' (POST /bots) and the transcript relay's numeric→native resolve
API key this control plane presents to the gateway (mint one via admin-api / `make all`)

DOCKER-HOST path to a claude credentials JSON. agent-api does not use it itself — the RUNTIME bind-mounts it into every spawned worker at /root/.claude/.credentials.json (see the runtime's config.v1) — but the agent plane's /health surfaces whether ANY model-credential path is configured, because that is where the operator looks when chat fails, and Settings → Models "Test" reads the mirrored file. PAIR IT WITH HOST_CLAUDE_DIR: the single-FILE mirror is inode-pinned and goes stale on the CLI's next token refresh

keys.default: (unset — only the legacy single-file mirror is available)
keys.description: DOCKER-HOST path of the claude config DIRECTORY (~/.claude), mirror-mounted READ-ONLY at /var/lib/vexa/host-claude. Settings → Models "Test" (control_plane.config_test) resolves .credentials.json inside it PER CALL. Same credential as HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS in the shape that survives a refresh: the CLI replaces the file via rename(2) (NEW inode) and a single-FILE bind stays pinned to the original inode, so this surface reported an already-refreshed token as expired for 32h (dogfood, 2026-08-31). Set it to the parent of HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS

Path to a codex subscription auth.json delivered into every spawned worker — compose bind-mounts it; on k8s/helm the runtime mounts it from a Secret (RUNTIME_K8S_SECRET_MOUNTS) and this key is set on agent-api purely so the model-credential capability reads configured (same surfacing-only semantics as HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS)
API-key credential path (brokered into workers by the runtime; surfaced here for the agent plane's /health row)
OAuth/OpenRouter-style bearer credential path (brokered into workers by the runtime; surfaced here for the agent plane's /health row)

claude CLI subscription OAuth token — the env-delivered credential path: dispatch stamps it (MODEL_AUTH_ENV_ALLOWLIST) into every worker spec env, the k8s/helm counterpart of the HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS mount
claude-CLI/gateway endpoint — an endpoint selector, not a credential alternative; dispatch stamps it (with the credential it pairs with) into every worker spec env
Lane M: identity admin-api base URL for the users.data.memberships[] index mirror; empty = in-memory index (policy/members.json in the workspace git repo stays authoritative)

meeting-api base URL — agent-api owner-scopes the live SSE feed (GET /api/meeting/stream) by hitting GET /meetings/{id} on it before opening the redis transcript stream (P0 cross-tenant leak fix, SSE sibling of the by-id ownership check). compose relies on the default service DNS name, helm sets it explicitly to the release-qualified Service DNS (unset it fails closed → 403 for the owner, #677), lite overrides to localhost

THE internal-tier shared secret — one name across every service (the compose/helm secret key). agent-api both PRESENTS it (Lane M: X-Internal-Secret on the admin-api membership-index edge) and BELIEVES it: `_internal_caller` compares this value, and gate 0 of the meeting room is by the code's own statement the trust boundary on who is in the room. Unset it used to mean `_internal_caller` simply returned False; the boot now refuses instead, because a half-configured internal tier is not a degrade an operator can see. Read through an alias so the deprecated VEXA_-prefixed spelling still works for one release (shared/config.py).

keys.default: (unset — DEPRECATED alias of INTERNAL_API_SECRET; read only when the canonical name is absent, and the boot logs a deprecation warning)
keys.description: DEPRECATED spelling of INTERNAL_API_SECRET. One secret had three names (INTERNAL_API_SECRET in compose/helm and in admin-api/gateway/meeting-api, VEXA_INTERNAL_API_SECRET here and in the terminal, VEXA_INTERNAL_SECRET in flows) and the drift is what let a placeholder survive on one spelling's refusal list and not the others (F95). No deploy surface sets it on agent-api any more; it is still READ so an operator mid-upgrade is warned rather than 401ed. Delete once the terminal reads the canonical name too.

keys.default: (unset — the post-meeting room resolves no participant and mounts ZERO desks)
keys.description: admin-api's ADMIN token, used for ONE question: resolve a meeting participant's email address to a subject for the post-meeting room (control_plane.meeting_room). The narrow door does not exist yet — agent-api's internal-secret tier on admin-api exposes no by-email lookup, and GET /admin/users/email/{email} sits behind this much broader credential (it can also create and patch users). Empty by DEFAULT and the room degrades to ZERO desks without it, never to matching a person by name. Delete this key once admin-api serves GET /internal/users/by-email/{email} returning only {id}: agent-api already prefers that route

keys.default: (unset — a first-visit scaffold reports no invited meetings rather than guessing)
keys.description: Read-only DSN for the meetings database, used for ONE question: which meetings is this email address invited to, read off data.attendees. It is the only record that knows somebody was invited BEFORE they ever signed in, which is exactly the case a first visit is — an owner-keyed lookup answers 'none' for the person this exists to serve. Unset, invited_meetings is absent from the scaffold and the opening says nothing about meetings rather than asserting there are none; emptiness and ignorance are different sentences to somebody reading their first screen. Delete this key once meeting-api serves an invited-by-address route, so agent-api stops holding a second database credential.
when true, reject callers lacking the gateway-signed X-Gateway-Verified identity marker (hardened multi-tenant topology); default false preserves dev/direct-edge access

Settings→Models Test button: the deployment-default STT backend URL probed by GET /api/transcription/test when no user/global override exists (the same env floor bot_spawn falls back to in meeting-api; rides in via env_file .env). Empty → the test reports 'no backend configured'
SECRET — the token paired with TRANSCRIPTION_SERVICE_URL for the on-demand /balance probe (Settings→Models Test). Never logged or echoed; only a pass/fail summary leaves the service

where a person's own terminal lives — the origin every scaffold link is built on (PRD §5.5). Deliberately the SAME variable name the flows lane already reads (core/flows/src/flows_steps/common.py UI_URL): one deployment fact, one name, because two spellings of a host is how a link ends up naming somewhere the person cannot reach. Unset, the mint route answers 503 rather than returning a url with no origin — a mint is what a step checks BEFORE it sends, and VEXA_UI_URL being set nowhere is exactly how every deeplink the rig ever minted pointed at a port nothing serves (PRD §3.3)

keys.default: (unset — no MCP is attached to a worker; the pre-delegation behaviour)
keys.description: the vexa-control MCP endpoint a spawned chat worker connects to (e.g. https://rig.dev.vexa.ai/mcp). Set together with VEXA_MCP_DELEGATION_SECRET: either alone leaves the toolbelt OFF, because an endpoint with no credential and a credential with no endpoint are both unusable

keys.default: (unset — delegation is OFF and no worker receives an MCP credential)
keys.description: the symmetric HS256 key agent-api SIGNS the per-dispatch MCP delegation token with and the vexa-control MCP VERIFIES with (shared.delegation). Empty must mean ABSENT, never 'signed with nothing' — a zero-length HMAC key would authenticate anyone who guessed the token format

keys.default: (empty — outside production a 0600 key is generated under the workspaces secrets root on first use, with a warning; in production an empty value is a boot refusal)
keys.description: server-side key the credential store seals with (saved GitHub PAT + per-workspace deploy-key private halves). EMPTY GENERATES ONE BESIDE THE CIPHERTEXT, under the workspaces secrets root — enough against a stray read, nothing against a stolen volume or a backup. It was settable on no deployment surface, so no deployment ever set it and every deployment quietly took the weaker property while the docs asserted the stronger one (R-E08). It is on compose and helm now, and with VEXA_ENV=production an unset value is a refusal naming the fix rather than a silent downgrade

the deployment profile, spelled as the mcp and transcription services already spell it (`transcription/main.py`, `vexa_mcp/app.py`): anything but the exact word `production`, including unset, is a development posture. agent-api reads it in ONE place — the credential store, where production turns an unset VEXA_SECRETS_KEY from a generated key beside the ciphertext into a refusal (R-E08)

lifetime of a minted MCP delegation token. It only has to outlast one dispatch's warm window, so it is deliberately short: a leaked worker env goes stale on its own rather than needing the human's own credential rotated

keys.default: (unset — derived per dispatch: minted by the dispatcher, never configured)
keys.description: the short-lived scoped delegation token the dispatcher stamps into the WORKER's env (subject + regime + workspace scope + exp + jti); the worker writes it into its gitignored .claude/mcp.json as an Authorization header. Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

keys.default: (unset — derived per dispatch: the subject the dispatch acts for)
keys.description: the PERSON this dispatch acts for — the quota and credential-brokerage axis, and the subject the worker's timeline preamble is scoped to (PRD decision 31). Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

flows-api's base url, for the WORKER's read-only timeline route (GET /timeline?format=preamble). Unset ⇒ the dispatch carries no temporal block and the turn behaves exactly as it did before decision 31

the READ-ONLY key that opens flows-api's GET /timeline and nothing else (flows_api._timeline_key). This is the one to set: VEXA_FLOWS_API_KEY is the OPERATOR key and would let every worker container submit and activate flows
flows-api's OPERATOR key. Read here only as a fallback credential for the timeline preamble; prefer VEXA_FLOWS_TIMELINE_KEY, which cannot configure the machine

how long a subject's rendered timeline block is reused across dispatches — fresh enough that a meeting that just ended is in the next turn, cheap enough that three messages in a row cost one round-trip
how long the worker waits for the timeline route before giving up on the block for this turn (a failure is cached like an answer)
how many past events the per-dispatch timeline block states (decision 31 §1: a handful of lines)
how many scheduled meetings the per-dispatch timeline block states

openai-agent harness: the OpenAI-compatible endpoint the turn's chat/completions run against. Falls back to ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, which is what a per-subject Settings → Models gateway arrives as — there is ONE endpoint pair and this is its second spelling, kept because the harness predates the collapse
openai-agent harness: the bearer token for VEXA_LLM_BASE_URL. Optional — a self-hosted vLLM behind the deployment's own network needs none. Falls back to ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN then ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

openai-agent harness: the model id, when it differs from the product-wide VEXA_AGENT_MODEL. VEXA_AGENT_MODEL is the one Settings → Models writes and the one the dispatch stamps, so this is an override and not the main dial

openai-agent harness: a JSON object merged into EVERY chat/completions request — the escape hatch for server-specific fields the OpenAI dialect cannot express. THE ONE DIAL WITH NO ANTHROPIC-DIALECT EQUIVALENT, and load-bearing: a self-hosted Qwen returns nothing parseable without {"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}, and a mis-stamped value fails SILENTLY (the turn runs with thinking on). Also settable per subject under Settings → Models
openai-agent harness: stream the completion (SSE). 0/false/no sends one blocking request per step instead — for an endpoint whose SSE is unreliable
openai-agent harness: hard per-turn ceiling on tool calls. A turn that reaches it stops and reports the truncation on its done event
openai-agent harness: hard per-turn wall-clock ceiling in seconds, reported the same way as the tool-call budget

openai-agent harness: estimated-token ceiling on the request. A SIZING RULE on a shared inference box rather than a nicety — a 24k-context request is about 1/29th of the CCC KV cache and an unbounded turn evicts everybody else

reasoning-effort pin passed to the claude-code CLI as --effort. Stamped per subject by the dispatch overlay (Settings → Models "effort"); empty leaves the CLI's own default, which OpenAI-compatible backends that validate reasoning_effort reject

codex harness: the model for the Codex app-server, when it differs from VEXA_AGENT_MODEL. Empty lets the signed-in subscription account choose, which is what stops a claude-* pin in Settings → Models from being fed to Codex

1 enables mid-turn user-message injection into a running harness turn (claude-code stream-json input, codex turn/steer). Off by default: an injection the harness drops is a message the person believes they sent
seconds a harness CLI subprocess is given to exit after its stream ends before it is killed
run the post-turn write-back phase (the entity/timeline bookkeeping that follows a chat turn). 0/false/off/no disables it
shortest turn worth a write-back phase, in estimated tokens — below it the bookkeeping costs more than it records
largest session transcript the worker will resume from; past it the thread starts a fresh harness session rather than re-sending an unaffordable history

the WORKER's warm-serve window: how long it keeps serving unit:<id>:in after its last turn. Dispatch-stamped per chat turn from VEXA_CHAT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SEC; the engine's own default is deliberately tighter
the allow-set a chat turn's harness is given (comma-separated). Runtime-injected per dispatch; the harness enforces it at EXECUTION, not only on the tool list it advertises
the conversation THREAD this dispatch belongs to — the worker namespaces its continuity session file by it, so several threads coexist in one user workspace. Runtime-injected per dispatch

keys.default: (unset — present only on a post-meeting room dispatch)
keys.description: the meeting this dispatch is the POST-MEETING RUN for, stamped when a room was authorised and absent on every other dispatch. Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface. The worker reads it for the three things decision 22 says a room run must not do: no entity write-back and no desk-README refresh against the subject's own desk (both committed there, moved HEAD, and failed the meeting on process_meeting's own detector — F103), and no bot verbs in the MCP allow-set for a meeting that is over (F104). A POSITIVE signal rather than an inference from the mount set, because a room whose other attendees have no desks yet resolves to zero room mounts — the small-team case — so the mount shape answers 'not a room run' on a run that is one
the dispatch's ``start`` object as JSON (the entrypoint ask or the session ref). Runtime-injected per dispatch, never a deploy surface

keys.default: (unset in agent-api — the runtime injects unit:<id>:out per dispatch)
keys.description: the per-dispatch output Stream (unit:<id>:out) the worker writes its UnitEvents to. Runtime-injected per dispatch; a worker without it cannot report anything and refuses to boot (mandatory in the WORKER, which refuses to run without it; agent-api stamps it and never reads it)

keys.default: (unset in agent-api — the runtime injects unit:<id>:in per dispatch)
keys.description: the per-dispatch input Stream (unit:<id>:in) the worker's serve loop reads interactive messages from. Runtime-injected per dispatch (mandatory in the WORKER, which refuses to run without it; agent-api stamps it and never reads it)

keys.default: (unset in agent-api — the runtime injects the worker's connection per dispatch)
keys.description: the WORKER's redis connection (its unit:<id>:in/out Streams). Runtime-injected per dispatch and deliberately withheld from the model's own subprocess (llm/ports._HARNESS_SUBPROCESS_DENY_VARS) — a Bash tool holding it reaches another tenant's keys (mandatory in the WORKER, which refuses to run without it; agent-api stamps it and never reads it)

bot_gateway.description: this control plane can call the gateway as a client — 'add bot from URL' + the transcript relay's numeric→native meeting-id resolve
bot_gateway.when_unconfigured: POST /api/meeting/bot fails loud; /api/meeting/relay-health reports a typed native_resolve error (kind=unauthorized/not-configured) instead of silent dead air

model_inference.description: spawned agent-workers will have a model-provider credential path available — dispatch stamps the model-auth allowlist from this service's env into every worker spec env (uniform across docker/k8s/process backends); the docker runtime additionally brokers/mounts creds itself (see the runtime's config.v1 for the mount mechanics + file probe)
model_inference.when_unconfigured: terminal chat / workspace turns fail inside the worker ('Model inference failed: Not logged in') — set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (subscription OAuth), an ANTHROPIC_* key, or HOST_CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS (docker subscription mount)
